question:
The following pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in manufacturing a scientific calculator. Study the pie chart and answer the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69248c7bbf88d1d2ff41184b01a1106fb5be823227641fd7181b1d27cd9faf51.png] 

If 500 products are manufactured and the direct labour cost on them amounts to Rs. 1,00,000, then what should be the selling price of the product so that the manufacturer can earn a profit of 44%?
solution:
**Given:**

Direct Labour Cost for 500 products = ₹1,00,000

**Formula used:**

Total Manufacturing Cost = Direct Labour Cost ÷ 0.24

Cost per Product = Total Manufacturing Cost ÷ Number of Products

Selling Price per Product = Cost per Product × (1 + Profit Percentage)
